_doc: Game taken in the valley (ADR-0027): what a deer or a hare gives up to a knife or an axe (data/wildlife carcass yields), and what the fire makes of it.

defs.name: Raw Venison
defs.description: Dark, lean haunch meat. Cook it: the Bloom is in the deer too, they say.

defs.name: Roast Venison
defs.description: Charred outside, pink in the middle. The best thing you've eaten since the drop.

defs.name: Raw Hare
defs.description: A skinned hare's hindquarters. Not much on it.

defs.name: Roast Hare
defs.description: Stringy and smoky. Worth the chase.

defs.name: Deer Hide
defs.description: A green hide, rolled hair-in. Scrape it, cut it into strips, or wear it against the cold.

defs.name: Hare Pelt
defs.description: Soft, thin, brown going white at the edges.

defs.name: Sinew
defs.description: Back-strap tendon, dried in strands. Stronger than any cord you can twist from fireweed.

defs.name: Hunting Bow
defs.description: A stave split from a straight branch, sinew-backed and strung with twisted sinew. Hold to draw, let go to loose; quiet enough to hunt with.

defs.name: Bone Arrow
defs.description: A straight shoot with a ground bone point bound on in sinew and split-fibre fletching. Heavier and keener than stone.

defs.name: Stone Arrow
defs.description: A straight stick, a knapped stone point lashed on with fibre, split-fibre fletching. Flies true enough; the point chips on bone.

defs.name: Rawhide Strips
defs.description: Hide cut in long strips. Wet it, wrap it, let it dry: it shrinks tight as iron.
